sources.entry: Flare - A nonbloated, modern, and highly configurable file/screenshot vault server with support for ShareX, Flameshot, and Spectacle. Offers OCR search and more. MIT Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Flare is a self-hostable, Next.js-based file and screenshot sharing server that works with ShareX, Flameshot, and KDE Spectacle.
summary.what_it_does: Flare is a file sharing platform meant to be self-hosted, built with Next.js. It accepts uploads from ShareX, Flameshot, KDE Spectacle, and a Bash script, and offers one-click configuration or script downloads for those tools. Files can be stored on the local filesystem or in S3-compatible storage, with optional OCR so images can be searched by their text. The README also describes a URL shortener, a pastebin, folders with shareable links, user roles with storage quotas, two-factor authentication and passkeys, and optional SSO via OIDC. Deployment uses Docker with PostgreSQL, and a Railway one-click option is also listed.
use_cases: share files with my team via links
host a URL shortener and pastebin
how_to_run: Follow the Docker Compose guide in the Flare documentation (PostgreSQL, persistent storage, generated secrets)
Alternatively, deploy with the Railway one-click button
Set the authentication secret and create an admin account after first deploy
notable: Works directly with ShareX, Flameshot, and KDE Spectacle upload workflows
OCR content search across uploaded images
Folders with one-link folder sharing and bulk file moves
Role-based permissions, storage quotas, and invite links
caveats: Requires a PostgreSQL server in addition to Docker
Documentation says the rolling tag tracks pre-releases, so pinned release tags are recommended for stable deployments
SSO does not yet support an explicit account-linking flow
